assets.title: Queue posts, then review performance
assets.content:
Subject: Queue posts, then review performance
Preview text: See whether Buffer Free has enough capacity for your weekly routine.

Queue this week’s posts, then review their performance

Hi there,

Buffer lets you queue a few posts across connected social channels, then review their performance in Insights. It’s social media management software for scheduling posts and inspecting the results in one place.

At the start of the week, add posts to each channel’s queue. After they publish, check recent engagement, impressions, and post performance before planning your next batch.

The Free forever plan supports up to three channels and 10 scheduled posts per channel at one time. Insights includes 30 days of history, so you can compare those limits with the routine you have in mind.

Check Buffer’s official plans to decide whether the Free entry fits your week.

Check Buffer’s official plans →

- the Buffer team

brief.orientation: Buffer is social media management software for scheduling posts across connected channels and reviewing their performance.
brief.arc: Introduce Buffer through one concrete weekly rhythm: queue a few posts, review basic results, then check whether the official Free plan limits fit that routine.
brief.sequence_rationale: One concise email is enough because the requested workflow, product introduction, Free-plan qualification, and next decision form one argument. emails.job: Help the reader decide whether Buffer's Free plan is a suitable way to try a weekly queue-and-review workflow.
emails.single_idea: At the start of the week, queue a few posts across connected channels; after they publish, use Insights to inspect recent engagement, impressions, and post performance before planning the next batch. Free supports this routine within explicit limits: up to three channels, ten scheduled posts per channel at one time, and thirty days of Insights history.
emails.felt_need: Plan a manageable week of social posts, then see which posts performed best.
emails.mechanism: Buffer combines a per-channel post queue with Insights beside the content it measures, so the reader can move from scheduling this week's posts to reviewing their recent performance in the same product.
emails.belief_shift: Before: Buffer is an abstract social media tool whose Free offer may be too vague to assess. After: it is a specific weekly queue-and-review workflow whose Free limits can be checked against the reader's needs.
must_not_say: Do not presume the reader currently uses another scheduling tool, spreadsheets, or manual posting.
Do not promise follower growth, audience growth, more engagement, time savings, or any guaranteed business result.
Do not claim or imply how quickly or easily a channel can be connected or a first post scheduled; setup time is not established.
Do not hide or soften the Free plan limits: up to 3 channels, 10 scheduled posts per channel at one time, and 30 days of Insights history.
Do not imply Free includes paid performance overviews, custom analytics, reports, unlimited history, or unlimited scheduled posts.
Do not imply every channel or account type supports identical publishing or analytics capabilities.
Do not turn the email into a broad feature list or introduce collaboration, AI, comments, integrations, or paid-plan pricing.
emails.objection: Will the Free plan actually cover a small weekly posting routine? Answer with the exact three-channel, ten-scheduled-posts-per-channel, and thirty-day Insights limits, leaving the reader to compare them with their needs.
emails.call_to_action: Check Buffer's official plans at https://buffer.com/pricing and consider the Free forever entry if its stated limits fit your week.
emails.next_step_decision: Whether Buffer Free has enough channel, queue, and Insights capacity for the reader's intended weekly routine.
emails.next_step_value: The official plans let the reader verify that Free supports up to three channels, ten scheduled posts per channel at one time, and thirty days of Insights history before choosing it.
emails.next_step_limit: Reviewing the plans does not establish setup time or confirm publishing and analytics behavior for the reader's specific social account types.
emails.subject_strategy: Make the recognizable weekly rhythm—queue first, review later—the reason to open, without hype, a growth promise, or a vague productivity claim.

brief.voice_notes: Use short, direct sentences centered on “you” and concrete actions. Keep the product name and the queue-to-Insights workflow unmistakable; describe the limits plainly rather than burying them in a footnote.
